about: Header-only Starfield plugins written by make_plugins.py from made-up bytes. Give the folder to the tool as its Data folder (or each file as its plugin input). 'answer' is the expected answer, 'masters' the master list a header reader must return (null when the header can't be read), 'kind' full, light, medium or light_or_warn.

answers.read: The tool reads the file as normal and gives its normal answer.
answers.finding: The tool's normal 'problem found' answer (its finding exit code) with a message that names the plugin and the problem.
answers.refuse: A plain refusal: the tool's refusal exit code (usually 2 or 3) and a message that names the file. Nothing else is lost.
answers.read_or_finding: Either answer, as the tool documents it.
answers.finding_or_refuse: Either answer, as long as the message names the file.

never: a .NET unhandled exception or stack overflow
an exit code of 128 or more, or a negative one
running past the case's time limit
reading a file outside the folder it was given

files.why: The control: a plain full master with no masters. Every tool must read it normally.
The plugin lists itself as a master. A checker names that as a problem and ends with its result line; a master walk must stop on a name it has already seen.
round3: sf-mod-check B1 (stack overflow in check and release)

files.why: CycleA masters CycleB and CycleB masters CycleA. The run must end, with the loop named or at least a result line.
round3: sf-load-order C1 (a master loop stopped every recommendation)

files.why: The other half of the CycleA pair.
The second master does not exist in the folder. The message names SharedTest-NotThere.esm as missing, not the plugin itself.
round3: BuildKit C5 (Open said the plugin itself is not in Data)

files.why: The same master is listed twice. Read it or name it, but never crash or count the master twice (Mutagen's test data has the same case).
A light (small) master, flags 0x101, as most real light masters have.
round3: sf-patch-day C3 (a light master counted as full)

files.why: Both the light and the medium bit (flags 0x501). Plugins made by the game rarely have it, but LOOT's Creation Kit-made small master does. Read it as light or warn about the two bits; never call it full.
Depends on one master of each kind, so a tool that numbers FormIDs or counts masters sees all three kinds.
The header ends with an XXXX marker and a 65,536-byte ONAM. A reader must take the size from XXXX; one that ignores it reads the ONAM bytes as subrecords.
round3: BuildKit C3 (the header reader does not handle XXXX)

files.why: XXXX claims 1,000,000 bytes but the record holds 64. Name the file as damaged; never read past the record.
A zero-length file. Refuse it, or report it as damaged, by name. A checker reports it (sf-mod-check 0.27.0: ERROR, exit 1).
Only the first 10 of the 24 record-header bytes.
The record header promises more bytes than the file holds.
A zip renamed to .esm (it does not start with TES4).

files.setup: Put a copy of SharedTest-Plain.esm named SharedTest-Outside.esm in the parent of the test folder; the tool must not read it.
files.why: A master name with a folder part. It must not lead the tool to a file outside the folder it was given.
round3: sf-mod-check S1 (note: master names such as ..\x.esm)

files.why: A missing master whose name holds U+202E. The finding must print it escaped (see terminal-text), so the line is not reordered.
round3: sf-mod-check B2 (check printed finding text without SafeText.OneLine)

files.why: A missing master whose name holds a line break, a made-up RESULT line and an escape code. The output must stay one line per finding with no raw control characters.
round3: papyrus-log-check C1 (a newline in a name added a fake PASS line)
